problem: CLI must display and annotate HTML reports alongside Markdown. The library show command parses headings from both formats and annotates with comment summaries.

files.why: Core report display. Line 48: HTML heading regex. Line 70: Markdown heading regex. Both paths extract slug and annotate with comment summary counts.
Router for library commands: list, show, comments.
Lists section-grouped comments for a report.
Posts ratings/comments on report sections. Uses slugify() for section anchor matching.
Build: tsc. No external markdown/HTML libraries — all parsing is custom regex.

facts: show.ts already handles both HTML and Markdown headings: HTML pattern at line 48, Markdown fallback at line 70
HTML heading regex extracts id attribute for slug, falls back to slugify(rawText) when no id present
HTML tag content is stripped of nested tags via .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '') before display
slugify() implementation differs slightly from client: CLI uses /[^a-z0-9\s-]/g while client uses /[^a-z0-9]+/g — could cause anchor mismatch on edge cases
CLI outputs HTML report headings as Markdown-style annotation (## Heading [slug] (N comments: ...)) regardless of source format
No external dependencies for HTML/Markdown parsing — all custom regex in TypeScript
Quality gates: npm run build (tsc), npm run typecheck, npm run test (node --test)
unknowns: Whether the CLI show.ts only outputs heading annotations and skips non-heading HTML lines — non-heading content appears to be silently dropped for HTML reports
Whether the slugify() difference between CLI and client causes any real-world anchor mismatches affecting comment targeting
Whether the HTML heading regex handles multi-line headings or headings with complex nested elements
